analyst_view.overall: Early view: Basaksehir (8th) under Nuri Sahin have scored seven in their last two games, 5-2 against Samsunspor and a comeback 2-1 at Goztepe with goals from Selke and Edin Visca. Corum (9th) lost 5-0 at home to Fenerbahce before the break, but the club president publicly backed coach Burak Yilmaz, whose side had taken nine points from the previous four games. Corum's Berat Ayberk Ozdemir is out for six to eight weeks with a calf strain.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.8 goals, which is high but fits these sides: Corum's eleven games have produced 42 goals and Basaksehir's 36. Corum may tighten up after the 5-0, but they scored three at Erzurumspor two weeks earlier, so they will create chances too, and I stay with the number.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.7 corners. Basaksehir should have more of the ball at home while Corum look to counter, which fits the 4.9 to 3.8 split, and I have nothing that moves the total.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.5 cards. Corum's Gokhan Sazdagi had to sit out the Fenerbahce game after a yellow-card build-up, but this is a Monday-night mid-table game with no rivalry, so I stay near the number.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.2 shots and I lean a little higher. Basaksehir's attack is in form, and Corum are more likely to come out and try to answer the heavy defeat than to sit in, which tends to open up both ends.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.7 shots on target. With both sides scoring freely this season that looks about right, and I would not move it until the lineups are known.
